name: Typewriter strike
sub: Each glyph is a separate strike: its own pressure, a slight offset and rotation, sometimes only half the face lands. Ink passes through a woven ribbon, so letters carry the ribbon's weave; the type bar also dents the paper — visible under a low light.

entry.call: fx.run(o, W, H, dpr, { S, clips })

in.o: params object — keys below; every length in CSS px
in.dpr: device px per CSS px (density is physical: marks per CSS px²)

x.S: params of every effect keyed by id; the stock this prints on is read from S[printsOn]
x.clips: Float32Array alpha per name (strikes), from FXSET.clips('fx-07-typewriter', W, H, dpr, o) on a thread with fonts
x.umask: optional: clips.umask — a typed or image mask (mShape type | image)

out.lin: Float32Array W·H·3, linear-light sRGB (encode with FX.toRGBA(R,"image",W,H))
out.ink: Float32Array W·H, absorbance / coverage (FX.toRGBA(R,"ink",…) = film positive)
out.stock: Float32Array W·H, stock height (FX.toRGBA(R,"stock",…) = normalized height map)

light.note: az = direction the light comes FROM (screen degrees; 0 = right, 90 = below); el = elevation above the sheet

deterministic: yes — every random draw is a hash of (position, seed); same inputs → same pixels in the same engine

params.label: Text
params.default: Four surfaces, one light. / Ink on real stock — counted, / never a gradient. Set 01.
params.note: "/" starts a new line

params.label: Key variance
params.note: how unevenly keys strike

params.label: Half strikes
params.note: share of glyphs where only the top or bottom lands

params.label: Ribbon wear
params.note: ink fading along the text

params.label: Ribbon texture
params.note: how much the ribbon weave shows in the glyphs

params.label: Ribbon count
params.note: ribbon threads per 100 CSS px

params.label: Ink squash
params.note: film pooling at the glyph edge

params.label: Impression
params.note: how deep each strike dents the stock

params.label: Prints on
params.note: paper = FX-03 live, cloth = FX-04 live, smooth = no substrate (film-splitting noise only). Tune the stock and this plate redraws.

params.label: Stock bite
params.note: how much the stock height (vs film-splitting noise) decides where ink lands

params.label: Break-up ↔ thin
params.note: 1 = ink film breaks into marks on the peaks as pressure falls; 0 = the film stays whole and thins to tone

params.label: Starve
params.note: the lowest share of the surface never takes ink — pinholes in the solid, placed by the paper's valleys and pits

params.label: Wick
params.note: ink carried along fibers into the run-out (hairline feathering)

params.label: Mottle
params.note: paper formation (its low-frequency cloudiness) varying the film thickness

params.label: Film split
params.note: clump size of the film-splitting noise (the roller's own speckle)

params.label: Ink · L
params.note: OKLCH lightness (0 black … 1 white)

params.label: Ink · C

limits.why: most hues leave sRGB above ~.26 and get chroma-reduced

params.note: OKLCH chroma; reduced at constant L/h if it leaves sRGB

params.label: Ink · h
params.note: OKLCH hue angle

params.label: Color rule
params.note: film = Beer–Lambert absorption in linear light (physical); oklab / oklch / linear / srgb = coverage mixes, for comparison

params.label: Seed
params.note: every random draw in the effect hangs off this one number

defaults.text: Four surfaces, one light. / Ink on real stock — counted, / never a gradient. Set 01.

recipe: Text in JetBrains Mono, one strike per glyph on the main thread: pressure = ribbon life (exhausting along the page) × key variance; offset, rotation, an occasional dropped baseline; half-strikes fade top or bottom.
Ribbon: a plain weave at the ribbon count — ink transfers through thread crossings, less through the gaps.
Ink chain: pressure × ribbon vs stock-height percentile; ink squash pools film at the glyph edge.
Impression: the strike dents the stock (blurred glyph × pressure); light from the combined height.

limits.what: weave reads as a screen pattern on the type
glyphs fall below the tooth scale and break up
